A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Multi-Modal Linkage (MML) research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v5.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack-success measurements, component ablations, decryption results, and defense experiments in Section 5 and the appendix.

after.justification: v5 retains those original results and adds timing measurements, a shift-cipher experiment, additional defense configurations, Llama-Guard evaluation, and o1 results.

M1.justification: v5 introduces MML-SC, an additional shift-cipher encoding and decoding variant, in Section 5.6 and Figure 19. The original four encoding methods, decryption hints, chain-of-thought prompting, and evil-alignment procedure remain; their complete appendix prompts are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate visual jailbreaks using SafeBench, MM-SafeBench, and HADES-Dataset, including defended SafeBench evaluation. The additions concern target models, evaluator-specific subsets, timing measurements, and prompt placement within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: FigStep and QueryRelated remain the comparators on SafeBench and MM-SafeBench, HADES remains the HADES-Dataset comparator, and FigStep remains the defense-experiment baseline. Added comparisons reuse these methods. Llama-Guard is introduced as an evaluator.

E3.justification: v5 adds Llama-Guard-3-8B evaluation using its unsafe-response criterion and subsets of 307, 867, and 687 instructions, respectively. It also adds o1 evaluation, timing protocols for 500 images and 10 fixed queries, and prefix/suffix AdaShield placements alongside the original infix configuration. The original main benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 3 are unchanged. v5 substantially expands analysis through defense-prompt placement sensitivity in Table 6, evaluator cross-validation in Appendix D.7, and encryption/inference efficiency analysis in Section 5.4.

E5.justification: The new timing experiment reports three independent runs, individual measurements, and averages in Table 5. This does not establish additional runs for the original attack-success experiments. Both versions retain five defense attack attempts and omit confidence intervals and seed information for their main ASR results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results, and v1's defense results reappear as the infix columns of v5 Table 6. Substantial additions include timing results, alternative-evaluator scores, prefix/suffix defense outcomes, MML-SC's 99.40% SafeBench ASR, and o1 results of 64.4% for MML-WR versus 34.8% for FigStep and 15.6% for QueryRelated. These are newly reported configurations, not improvements to unchanged experiments.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs. The threat-model assumptions and existing mathematical content remain unchanged; the added cipher description and clarification that encryption is metaphorical do not introduce formal theory.

C1.justification: The central framework and contribution claims remain. The abstract and introduction raise the headline GPT-4o SafeBench success claim from 97.80% to 99.40%, reflecting the new shift-cipher variant, and the introduction updates the corresponding baseline advantage from 64.80 to 66.4 percentage points.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly qualifies encryption-decryption as metaphorical, explains runtime differences through image size and response length, and discusses possible single-evaluator bias. It removes the earlier inability-to-test-o1 limitation. The central safety-alignment interpretation and vulnerability to output detection remain.

D1.justification: v5 supplies the full shift-cipher prompt, three defense-prompt forms, and timing implementation information, including Apple M1 Pro hardware and image sizes. The original code-access information, replacement-word lists, four method prompts, and preprocessing instructions remain, with some details relocated to Appendix D.

R1.justification: v5 removes the dedicated LLM-jailbreak related-work subsection and AutoDAN reference, while adding references including RTVLM, McCoy et al., Llama 3, and VLM applications. The paper's central positioning around structure-based attacks remains unchanged; Zeng et al. was already credited in v1.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method explanations receive extensive rewriting. Baseline descriptions and preprocessing move into the appendix, the appendix is reorganized into sections A–F with detailed D subsections, and ethics, limitations, and acknowledgments become separate main-text sections.

P2.justification: v5 redesigns Figure 1, adds six result tables, expands the defense table into three placement conditions, and adds shift-cipher and defense-prompt panels. Existing plots and tables are redistributed. Figure 11 is reworked, correcting mismatched example categories and changing how response excerpts are displayed.

improvement.justification: v1's effectiveness evidence relied on one LLM evaluator and one AdaShield placement. v5 substantially strengthens validation through a second evaluator on documented subsets and defense-placement tests, while adding measured costs and an o1 evaluation (Tables 4–6 and 9–11). These gains improve the credibility and practical scope of the conclusions. Reporting defects remain: the defense discussion emphasizes infix results, and the stated 29.6-point o1 'average' advantage actually matches the best variant's advantage over FigStep.
